study_identification_part.si_4_title: GPT-based normative models of brain sMRI correlate with dimensional psychopathology

nm2_1_modeling_methods.answer: Deep Learning: VQ-VAE; Deep Learning: GPT
nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used a two-stage architecture: (1) Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) to reduce brain MRI dimensions from ~14.2 million voxels to 16,128 latent discrete codes, and (2) Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT, also called autoregressive Transformer) to model the probability density function of the typical brain based on the serialized discrete codes. Nine GPT models were trained from different views and ensembled for predictions.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The architecture used in both studies is composed of two models. The first, called Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE), is responsible for reducing the size of the input MRI from millions of voxels to a representation of thousands of latent discrete codes. The second, a Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) (also known as autoregressive Transformer) uses the encoded representation generated by the VQ-VAE to learn a probability density function of the typical brain.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study used T1-weighted structural MRI (sMRI) preprocessed via Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) with SPM12. The preprocessing produced gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM) tissue maps with dimensions of 181x217x181 voxels at 1mm3 resolution. Both GM and WM were used as input to ensure only brain tissue data would be delivered to the neural networks.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The collected sMRI were preprocessed using the Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM)... Therefore, the preprocessed sMRI resulted in two matrices (i.e., GM and WM), each with a dimension of 181x217x181 voxels. We considered only the GM and WM to ensure that only brain tissue data would be delivered to the neural networks, eliminating the risk of biasing the models due to learning from non-brain tissues.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model architecture (VQ-VAE + GPT) does not use explicit explanatory variables (covariates) such as age or sex. The model learns a typicality pattern directly from the brain images of typically developing subjects in an unsupervised manner. The GPT models the probability of occurrence of each discrete code based on the learned context from the training data, without incorporating demographic or other covariates as explicit predictors.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: As these models use unsupervised methods, they have the advantage of not depending on labeled or anomaly examples in the training phase... Like in the referenced work, our approach is normative as we use only typical subjects (i.e., normal) to train the models. In the test phase, both atypical and typical subjects are evaluated.
